# Automatic module name starting with number

There can be cases where the project must be built with only Java 1.8 and thus
cannot take advantage of
[JEP 238: Multi-Release JAR Files](https://openjdk.org/jeps/238). In this case,
it is recommended to define the module name in the `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file.
While the Java module system can determine the module name automatically from
the JAR file name, that is less than ideal as the file name can easily change.
Also, providing the module name would eliminate any guess work as the module
name will be simply read from the `Automatic-Module-Name` entry in the
`META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file.

```text
Main-Class: demo.Main
Automatic-Module-Name: 123.invalid.name
```

This simple example shows how to provide the module name in the
`META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file using the [Maven](https://maven.apache.org/) build
tool.

```xml
<plugin>
    <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
    <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>${maven-jar-plugin.version}</version>
    <configuration>
        <outputDirectory>${project.build.directory}/libs</outputDirectory>
        <archive>
            <manifestFile>src/main/resources/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF</manifestFile>
        </archive>
    </configuration>
</plugin>
```

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR file

   ```
   ./target/libs
   └── automatic-module-name-starts-with-number.jar

   1 directory, 1 file
   ```

2. Describe the JAR file

   The automatic module name is fetched from the name `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`
   that we defined in the `[MANIFEST.MF]` file, which is copied by the
   `maven-jar-plugin` plugin.

   ```xml
   <plugin>
       <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
       <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
       <version>${maven-jar-plugin.version}</version>
       <configuration>
           <outputDirectory>${project.build.directory}/libs</outputDirectory>
           <archive>
               <manifestFile>src/main/resources/META-INF/MANIFEST.MF</manifestFile>
           </archive>
       </configuration>
   </plugin>
   ```

   Difference from the example shown in the
   [automatic-module-name](../automatic-module-name/README.md) project, we
   cannot use the `Automatic-Module-Name`, as otherwise the `maven-jar-plugin`
   will fail, with an error similar to the one shown below.

   ```
   [ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.apache.maven.plugins:maven-jar-plugin:3.5.1:jar (default-jar) on project automatic-module-name-starts-with-number: Error assembling JAR: Invalid automatic module name: '123.invalid.name' -> [Help 1]
   ```

   The `Automatic-Module-Name` is defined in the `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF` file
   that was created by Maven.

   ```shell
   unzip -p './target/libs/automatic-module-name-starts-with-number.jar' 'META-INF/MANIFEST.MF'
   ```

   This will print the contents of the manifest file

   ```
   Manifest-Version: 1.0
   Created-By: Maven JAR Plugin 3.5.1
   Java-Version: 25
   Build-Jdk-Spec: 25
   Main-Class: demo.Main
   Automatic-Module-Name: 123.invalid.name
   ```

   Describe the JAR file

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/automatic-module-name-starts-with-number.jar'
   ```

   The module description cannot be extracted from the JAR file due to an
   invalid automatic module name.

   ```
   Unable to derive module descriptor for: ./target/libs/automatic-module-name-starts-with-number.jar
   Automatic-Module-Name: 123.invalid.name: Invalid module name: '123' is not a Java identifier
   ```

3. Run the application

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --module 123.invalid.name
   ```

   Given the application has an invalid automatic module name, this JAR file
   cannot be included as an automatic module.

   ```
   Error occurred during initialization of boot layer
   java.lang.module.FindException: Unable to derive module descriptor for ./target/libs/automatic-module-name-starts-with-number.jar
   Caused by: java.lang.module.FindException: Automatic-Module-Name: 123.invalid.name: Invalid module name: '123' is not a Java identifier
   ```

   On the other hand, the application works well when loaded as an unnamed
   module, that is using the class path (`--class-path`) instead.

   ```shell
   java --class-path './target/libs/*' demo.Main
   ```

   The JAR file is loaded as an unnamed module and the automatic module name
   ignored.

   ```
   Invalid Automatic Module Name
   Using Java 25.0.4.1
   ```
